messages:
Sam: Heads up — I ran a focused bench on fused attention changes from last week's PR and we're seeing a regression on A100 for long sequences. seq=1024, batch=8 throughput down ~12%, latency +18ms overall.
Lina: ugh. which change looked suspicious? qkv packing or the post-attention combine step?
Sam: both touched. The pack reorder to reduce memcpy seemed fine for short seqs, but profile shows heavy stalls in the write-back path (the post-attn add/proj).
Devon: can you paste the perf output?
Sam: sure — here's the core numbers from perf-bench: 
```
model: gpt-like, seq=1024, heads=16, d_head=64
old-fused: throughput=320 tok/s, p50=42ms
new-pack: 281 tok/s, p50=60ms
flash-v2 baseline: 295 tok/s
```
Rashmi: that looks like ~12% reg as you said. perf-bot, did you upload flamegraph? :eyes: 
perf-bot: uploaded flamegraph to https://ci/internal/fg/1780123456 — top stacks show heavy time in `attention_postproc_kernel` and `memcpy_async` waits.
Lina: interesting — maybe QKV packing impacted memory coalescing for the projection write. Did the new pack change the output layout?
Sam: yes — we switched from packed [B, H, S, D] to interleaved [B, S, H, D] to optimize GEMM order. That helped small seq but seems to create bank conflicts when the post-attn kernel writes back per-head slices.
Devon: could be cache line striding. Also the KV cache path (paged attention) shows higher latency on cache hits for the same variant. Any numbers?
Sam: paged-attn hit path: avg write latency +22% when packing enabled. Probably due to scatter pattern into the global KV store.
Rashmi: hypothesis: packing improved local GEMM but moved work to the epilogue-like projection which isn't fused now. If we fuse the bias+rope+proj add inside the attention output kernel we could recover.
Lina: agreed. Two short experiments: 1) revert packing order to previous output layout but keep internal pack for GEMM (cheap copy), 2) fuse bias+rope into the post-attn kernel. Which is faster to try?
Devon: 1) is trivial and low risk — let's try that to confirm packing is culprit. 2) is more invasive but may give net win. I'll queue a small patch for (1).
Sam: patch in my branch: `revert-output-layout.patch` — bench after revert looks promising: throughput=310 tok/s, p50=46ms (almost back).
Rashmi: nice. So packing was the regression vector. For (2) fusion notes: we should avoid increasing register pressure too much. If bias+rope fusion pushes us above register file limit on A100 we might get spilling. Need microbench.
Lina: also try a lightweight epilogue merge: do bias add and rope in-place before the projection, but keep projection separate. That reduces memory traffic without huge register blowup.
Sam: good call. I'll prototype in-place bias+rope and run microbench at seq 512/1024, batch 4/8.
perf-bot: FYI — I ran automated kernel-selection loop across variants and it defaulted to new-pack for seq<=256 and old-pack for seq>=512 based on microcost. We may need to tweak heuristics to prefer old-pack for long-seq on A100.
Devon: update routing heuristics: add a rule to pick output-layout variant by (device, seq_threshold, head_size). Also add a KV-cache-aware penalty if paged-attn enabled.
Rashmi: I'll draft the heuristic change. Also adding a small unit test to ensure we don't pick the regressed variant for production configs.
Lina: one more thought — quantify quality of fusion vs register pressure: make a 2D grid (reg pressure vs throughput) and pick sweet spot per-device. We can store that in the model-profile metadata.
Sam: agreed. Action items: 
- Devon: revert-output-layout hotfix PR and gating benchmark (in review) — ETA today.
- Sam: prototype in-place bias+rope fusion microkernel and collect flames — ETA tomorrow EOD.
- Rashmi: heuristic tweak + test to prefer safe variant for seq>=512 on A100 — ETA tomorrow.
- Lina: coordinate canary rollout once hotfix lands.
perf-bot: noted tasks and will re-run the nightly perf matrix after PR merges.
Devon: thanks — let's keep the thread updated with flamegraphs and numbers. :thumbsup:
